mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered months, or the effect is absent during periods of strong wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during periods of strong export growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month averages in at least 70% of cases, or the effect reverses during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 3% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > 3% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong credit expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a stable or declining unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tight labor market with limited slack, which supports wage growth and ultimately drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average and UNRATE <= 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of rapidly rising inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average, while personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) stagnate, signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a consumer-driven economic slowdown and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months AND GDPC1 flat (change < 0.5% month-over-month) for same period
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong corporate investment.
